policy:
Labeling policy (applied in order):
P1 Data first. If the target's count is unverified, flagged (reportFlag), stale (>10 days), already under recount,
   or contradicts its own dispensing trend (recorded daily use far from the weekly trend), the next step is
   verify_count. Moving or ordering stock on a bad count wastes scarce stock.
P2 Transfer. If a verified donor's transferable surplus (already net of its 7-day reserve and open outbound
   transfers) covers the target's gap (coversGapPct >= 100), choose transfer_surplus. Near-expiry donor stock
   is preferred because it would otherwise be wasted.
P3 Unverified donors do not count as surplus.
P4 Escalate. If verified local surplus cannot cover the gap and upstream supply is delayed or unavailable, or the
   district store holds less than one lead time of district demand, choose escalate_supply_gap.
P5 Indent. If verified local surplus cannot cover the gap and upstream supply is normal, choose draft_indent.
Ambiguous. Cases where two rules reasonably compete (partial cover 60-99%, combined cover from two donors,
   a full transfer while upstream is indefinitely delayed, an unverified zero count with patients waiting,
   zero recorded use) are tagged ambiguous with the acceptable alternatives listed.

configs.instructions: Choose the single safest next operational step for the target facility. Consider report verification (verified flag, reportFlag, report age), days of stock against the resupply lead time plus safety buffer, inbound transfers, donor surplus after its reserve, and whether the action can bridge the gap. Prefer a local transfer when a verified donor has sufficient surplus and preserve every donor's reserve. Do not treat a transfer as a cure for upstream shortages: when upstream supply is delayed or unavailable and local surplus cannot cover the gap, escalate. The officer must approve all actions. If the snapshot contains a counterfactual field, judge that hypothetical scenario as stated.

Choose the single safest next operational step for the target facility. Consider report verification (verified flag, reportFlag, report age), days of stock against the resupply lead time plus safety buffer, inbound transfers, donor surplus after its reserve, and whether the action can bridge the gap. Prefer a local transfer when a verified donor has sufficient surplus and preserve every donor's reserve. Do not treat a transfer as a cure for upstream shortages: when upstream supply is delayed or unavailable and local surplus cannot cover the gap, escalate. The officer must approve all actions. If the snapshot contains a counterfactual field, judge that hypothetical scenario as stated.
Choose the next action for the target facility.

Choose the single safest next operational step for the target facility. Apply these checks in order and stop at the first that holds. 1) If the target's count is unverified, has a reportFlag, is under recount, or its dailyUse is far from weeklyDispensedTrend divided by 7, choose verify_count. 2) If one verified donor's transferable units (already net of its own reserve) cover the target's gapUnits (coversGapPct 100), choose transfer_surplus. A donor that covers only part of the gap does not qualify, and unverified donors never count. 3) If no verified donor covers the gap and upstream status is delayed or unavailable, or districtStore.daysOfDistrictDemand is below the medicine's leadTimeDays, choose escalate_supply_gap. 4) Otherwise choose draft_indent. The officer must approve all actions.
